package_info.why_malicious: The entire package is designed to covertly surveil victims by exfiltrating SMS messages (including 2FA codes), recording ambient audio, stealing contacts and account data, enumerating installed apps and running processes, and presenting phishing UIs to steal credentials. It masquerades as a legitimate service but performs extensive unauthorized data collection and exfiltration to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

execution_context.file_location: Android app main service (background receiver for SMS events)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when an SMS is received, the code intercepts the message, extracts its content, and forwards it to a hardcoded attacker-controlled phone number via SMS, resulting in real-time exfiltration of sensitive messages such as 2FA codes.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting and forwarding all incoming SMS messages, especially those containing 2FA codes, to an external number is a clear indicator of credential theft and surveillance activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate app should never forward private SMS messages to third parties without explicit, informed user consent and clear notification.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Parental control or enterprise monitoring apps may intercept SMS, but only with user awareness, consent, and strict privacy controls.
key_indicators: Intercepts all incoming SMS messages via broadcast receiver
Forwards SMS content to a hardcoded external phone number
Requires RECEIVE_SMS, READ_SMS, SEND_SMS, and INTERNET permissions
No user notification or consent for SMS forwarding

execution_context.file_location: Android app background service (audio recording module)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, upon receiving a remote command from the C2 server, the code activates the device microphone, records ambient audio, saves the recording to a file, and uploads the audio file to the attacker's server, enabling covert surveillance.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Covertly recording audio in the background and exfiltrating the recordings to an external server is a hallmark of spyware and surveillance malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate apps must request explicit user permission, provide clear notification when recording audio, and never upload recordings without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Voice memo or call recording apps, but only with user consent, notification, and clear privacy policies.
key_indicators: Background audio recording triggered by remote command
No user interaction or notification during recording
Automatic upload of audio files to remote C2 server
Requires RECORD_AUDIO, WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE, and INTERNET permissions

execution_context.trigger: runtime (on command from C2 or at app startup)
execution_context.file_location: Android app background service (contacts and accounts exfiltration module)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, either on command from the C2 server or at app startup, the code collects all contacts and account information from the device and transmits this data to the attacker's server, resulting in bulk exfiltration of sensitive personal and account data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Harvesting all contacts and account data without user knowledge or consent is a severe privacy violation and enables further social engineering or credential attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate apps should only access contacts or accounts for core functionality, with explicit user consent and clear privacy disclosures.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Contact backup or sync apps, but only with user opt-in, clear privacy policy, and secure data handling.
key_indicators: Bulk collection of all contacts and account information
Network exfiltration of sensitive data to attacker infrastructure
No user notification or consent for data access or transmission
Requires READ_CONTACTS, GET_ACCOUNTS, and INTERNET permissions

execution_context.trigger: runtime (on command from C2 or at scheduled intervals)
execution_context.file_location: Android app background service (device info and app/process enumeration module)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, either on command from the C2 server or at scheduled intervals, the code enumerates all installed applications and running processes on the device, then sends this inventory to the attacker's server, enabling device profiling and tailored attacks.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Enumerating installed apps and running processes and exfiltrating this information is commonly used for reconnaissance, evasion, and targeting further attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal apps do not require full inventory of installed apps or running processes unless for device management or security purposes, and should always inform the user.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Device management or antivirus apps, but only with user awareness, consent, and clear justification.
key_indicators: Bulk enumeration of installed applications and running processes
Network exfiltration of device inventory to attacker infrastructure
Triggered by remote command or scheduled task
Requires QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES and INTERNET permissions

execution_context.file_location: Android app activity (Google account phishing screen)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
<WebView ...>
  loadUrl('https://malicious-phishing-site.com/google-login')
</WebView>
// Collect credentials entered and send to C2
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the user interacts with the phishing UI, the app presents a fake Google login page in a WebView, captures the credentials entered by the user, and sends them to the attacker's server, resulting in credential theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Presenting a fake login page to capture user credentials is a classic phishing technique and is always malicious.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate apps should redirect users to official OAuth flows for authentication, never embed fake login forms or intercept credentials.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; credential phishing via fake login UIs is inherently malicious.
key_indicators: Fake login UI presented in embedded WebView
WebView loads non-official login page (phishing domain)
Captured credentials are sent to attacker-controlled server
Requires INTERNET permission

attack_chain.action: Victim installs the malicious Android app, believing it to be a legitimate service.
attack_chain.leads_to: App requests and obtains broad permissions.

attack_chain.action: App requests permissions for SMS, contacts, audio recording, and other sensitive features.
attack_chain.leads_to: App is able to access sensitive data and device features.

attack_chain.action: App intercepts incoming SMS messages and forwards them to the attacker.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives 2FA codes and other sensitive SMS content.

attack_chain.action: App records ambient audio on command and uploads it to the attacker.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to victim's surroundings and conversations.

attack_chain.action: App exfiltrates contacts and account information to the attacker.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker can perform social engineering or further attacks using stolen data.

attack_chain.action: App enumerates installed apps and running processes, sending data to the attacker.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker can tailor further attacks or evade detection based on device inventory.

attack_chain.action: App presents a phishing UI to steal Google account credentials from the user.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker obtains credentials for further compromise of victim's accounts.

behavioral_signatures: Background interception and forwarding of SMS messages to external phone numbers
Covert audio recording and network exfiltration of audio files
Bulk exfiltration of contacts, accounts, and device inventory data
Enumeration of installed apps and running processes without user consent
Presentation of phishing UIs in embedded WebViews for credential theft
file_indicators: Android APKs requesting excessive permissions (RECEIVE_SMS, READ_SMS, SEND_SMS, RECORD_AUDIO, READ_CONTACTS, GET_ACCOUNTS, QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES, INTERNET)
Presence of code for SMS interception and forwarding via SmsManager
Embedded WebView components loading non-official login pages
Use of MediaRecorder for background audio capture
network_indicators: Outbound SMS messages sent to unknown or international phone numbers
HTTP/HTTPS POST requests to attacker-controlled C2 domains
Connections to domains or IPs associated with phishing infrastructure
Uploads of audio, contact, or account data to untrusted remote servers
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Android apps requesting broad and unrelated permissions, especially those involving SMS, audio, contacts, and accounts. Analyze app code for broadcast receivers handling SMS_RECEIVED and forwarding messages via SmsManager. Inspect for use of MediaRecorder in background services and for WebViews loading non-official login pages. Monitor network traffic for outbound SMS to suspicious numbers and data exfiltration to untrusted domains. Use mobile security solutions to flag apps exhibiting these behaviors and cross-reference with known indicators of compromise (IOCs).
